speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a chest skin lesion; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or shape recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The patient is a 63-year-old male with a growing, asymptomatic chest lesion and significant comorbidities (diabetes, hypercholesterolemia) that increase skin cancer risk. While basal cell carcinoma is common on the trunk, the rapid growth and lack of pain/itching in an elderly patient strongly favor Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Next, I will request a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy of Chest Lesion.
